1 outset, that the present petition has been filed with the relief to seek benefit of multiplication Factor 2 instead of Factor 1, on the ground that the lands in question lying in a rural area and the competent authority / Special Land Acquisition Officer is required to re-calculate the compensation by applying multiplication Factor 2 along with the other statutory benefits including Solatium and additional compensation under Section 30 of The Right to Fair Compensation and NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/2484/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/02/2026 undefined Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, "the Act' 2013"), besides other benefits such as interest for the delayed payment of compensation as per Section 80 of the Act' 2013.

2. Ms.Archana Amin, the learned advocate appearing for the respondent Railways, at the outset,
would submit that the respondent has no objection in redetermination / recomputation of compensation by applying multiplication Factor 2 with respect to the lands and the statutory benefits under Section 30 of the Act' 2013, namely the Solatium and additional compensation.

However, on the interest under Section 80, it is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for the Railways that the petitioners have approached this Court for the first time with a substantial delay,
inasmuch, the present petition has been presented on 17.12.2024, whereas the original award was passed on 02.04.2016.

3. The contention is that the dispute with respect to the payment of multiplication Factor 2 has been determined by this Court in the judgment and order dated 12.09.2019 passed in the the Special Civil Application No.8734 of 2019 with allied matters.

On a Special Leave Petition filed by the State Government, being SLP (C) Diary No.18777 of 2020, with the dismissal of the SLP vide the judgment and order dated 07.01.2021, the Division Bench judgment dated 12.09.2019 of this Court stood confirmed.

4. The submission is that inspite of the said determination made by this Court, wherein multiplication Factor 2 has been made available to the lands lying in the rural areas in the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/2484/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/02/2026 undefined State with the quashing of the Government resolutions dated 09.02.2016 and 29.07.2016, the petitioner had never laid his claim.
The entire writ petition is silent about any efforts made by the petitioner to seek compensation by application of Factor 2, prior to filing of the present petition.

5. Attention of this Court is invited to the statement made in the writ petition wherein the petitioner only stated to have made a representation dated 08.10.2024 to the competent authority / Special Land Acquisition Officer for seeking application of Factor 2.
6.

From the averments made in the writ petition and the material placed before us, it is evident that the petitioner had kept silence for a substantial period from 2019 till October, 2024, in the matter of seeking benefit of multiplication Factor 2.
There is no whisper in the writ petition that the petitioners had approached even the competent authority / Special Land Acquisition Officer prior to 08.10.2024.

sentences.text:
For the aforesaid, the liability of interest cannot be saddled upon the acquiring body for the period of delay / laches on the part of the petitioners.
8.

We, therefore, provide that:-
i.

The petitioners shall be entitled to multiplication Factor 2 and the redetermination of the compensation under the original award dated 02.04.2016 with respect to the land of the petitioner herein is required to be made by application of multiplication Factor 2, in accordance with the provisions of the Act' 2013.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/2484/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/02/2026 undefined

ii. All statutory benefits on the difference of the market value, recomputed by application of multiplication Factor 2 under the Act' 2013, shall also be included in the award for redetermination, to be made under this order.

iii. However, the liability of interest @ 9% and 15% under the scheme of Section 80 of the Act' 2013 is confined for the period from the date of taking possession till the expiry of period of three (3) years from the date of the judgment and order dated 12.09.2019 passed by the Division Bench of this Court passed in Writ Petition namely Special Civil Application No.8734 of 2019 with allied matters.

Beyond the said period, in our considered opinion, the petitioners are not entitled for interest under Section 80 as they have not approached this Court within a reasonable time even after the judgment and order dated 12.09.2019 passed by the Division Bench has been affirmed by the Apex Court with the dismissal of the SLP vide judgment and order dated 07.01.2021.
9. Subject to the above, the present petition stands disposed of.
